must_know.headline: Iran leaves Doha talks as draft US deal circulates, with US midterms and possible strikes looming
must_know.summary: Iranian negotiators have left Doha after three days of talks with Qatari mediators, and a draft proposal for a deal with the US is being circulated, an official told Reuters. The basis is a seven-step plan Tehran drew up in September to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the US naval blockade. Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said no final conclusion had been reached on a "two-day proposal" to reopen the strait after an agreement with Washington.
must_know.why_it_matters: Trump has said the US will not attack before the Nov. 7 vote but has not ruled out strikes afterwards, so the draft has about a day of political cover before the pause may end; Iran says any new war could run longer than the last.

reporting_varies.angle: Stresses the threat of renewed war: Trump says one or two sites remain to be hit "in 10 minutes", and Iran's army warns a new war could last longer.
Focuses on Gulf states bracing for escalation, with diplomats warning renewed conflict would be more damaging than earlier rounds.

must_know.headline: France opens attempted murder probe after petrol bomb hits police; school blockades resume The measure was announced in Geneva.
must_know.summary: French authorities opened an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during Paris protests, with footage of an officer engulfed in flames. Hundreds were arrested over the third straight weekend of protests over living costs and education. On Monday, Nov. 2, 41 high schools were blocked, Le Monde reported, as students returned from holidays despite government concessions announced the week of Oct. 26.
must_know.why_it_matters: Street violence is now being treated as attempted murder, while the student movement that began the protests is trying to restart even after the government's concessions, so the dispute is shifting from a bargaining issue to a law-and-order one.

reporting_varies.angle: Describes largely peaceful protests, with more than 320,000 people on the streets and tear gas used by police in some places.
Calls the weekend's toll devastating despite falling turnout: 515 fires, 779 arrests and 116 injured officers, and says a fourth week of protests looms.

must_know.headline: Belgian PM De Wever goes to king to resign after coalition fails to agree budget
must_know.summary: Prime Minister Bart De Wever went to the Royal Palace on Monday and was widely expected to offer his resignation, Belgian media reported, after late-night talks in his five-party coalition again failed to agree on next year's budget. The government has argued for months over €21bn ($11.2bn) in cuts and tax increases. De Tijd cited sources saying King Philippe was not expected to accept at once and could send him back for a last round of talks.
must_know.why_it_matters: The split is over how to close the gap: De Wever's N-VA and the liberal MR want spending cuts, including on healthcare, while their socialist and centrist partners want higher wealth taxes, and the collapse comes as bond yields for weak-finance European states have risen sharply.

should_know.headline: German ministers vow tough penalties after youth cost-of-living protest turns violent in Frankfurt
should_know.summary: At least 54 people, aged 13 to 29, were arrested in Frankfurt after rioters damaged 17 shops, five of them looted, late Saturday, according to Hesse interior minister Roman Poseck. More than 100 of 1,300 deployed police officers were injured. The riots followed largely peaceful rallies by the group "Gen Z regelt" in dozens of cities over education and living costs; violence also broke out in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg. Federal Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt promised "tough penalties" and blamed violent left-wing groups and troublemakers from the migrant community. Poseck said police estimate 1,000 to 1,500 violent troublemakers, predominantly of migrant background.

should_know.headline: Bulgaria's Iotova wins presidential runoff, becoming first elected female president
should_know.summary: Acting President Iliana Iotova won Bulgaria's presidential runoff, near-final results from the Central Election Commission showed on Monday. She becomes the country's first elected female president. Iotova favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, and the pro-European challenger had done unexpectedly well in the first round. Turnout was reportedly low, and the post is largely ceremonial.

should_know.headline: Saudi air defences down Houthi missile as coalition strikes Hodeidah port and oil site
should_know.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at southern Saudi Arabia on Monday. Civil defence had issued, then lifted, alerts for Abha, Khamis Mushait, Taif and Najran. Houthi-affiliated media said coalition strikes on Hodeidah's Ras Isa port and an oil company site in Bajil wounded seven people; the coalition did not comment. The Saudi economy shrank 3.8% as oil output fell, the Wall Street Journal reported.

should_know.headline: More than 300,000 flee renewed Yemen fighting as Houthis besiege Taizz
should_know.summary: More than 300,000 people have fled fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in western Yemen, the UN's migration agency said on Sunday. Nearly all left their homes in the past two months. Human Rights Watch says Taizz, which residents say the Houthis now fully besiege, lacks fuel, food, water and medicine. Separately, rights experts are urging an independent inquiry into the death in Houthi custody of UN human rights office employee Mohammad el-Shami, held since June 2024. He is the second UN staff member to die in Houthi custody, according to Al Jazeera.

should_know.headline: Binance users pull billions as exchange reopens after $6.3bn hack, with withdrawals reported to be slowing
should_know.summary: Customers withdrew about $3.64bn, or 2.1% of Binance's assets, on Sunday as the exchange came back online after the hack, according to Reuters. Binance says the rush is slowing. The Financial Times put the total at $5bn, and France 24 at $3.4bn. Binance has pledged to reimburse users whose assets were stolen in the hack, which the FBI links to North Korea.

should_know.headline: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years, as liquidation begins
should_know.summary: The UN mission in Western Sahara, known as MINURSO, ceased operations on Sunday after the Security Council failed to renew its mandate. Russia vetoed a US draft resolution on Friday, and a rival Russian text to extend the mission was then voted down. Morocco welcomed the end of the mission; the Algeria-backed Polisario Front called it "unacceptable", and the UN said Nov. 1 began a liquidation period in which a smaller team will oversee the return of assets to troop-contributing countries.

should_know.headline: Trump says US and Canada have a 'concept' of a trade deal, including a pipeline, after talking to Carney
should_know.summary: President Trump said the US and Canada have a "concept" of a new trade deal, after speaking with Prime Minister Mark Carney. Reuters reported the outline includes a pipeline. Trade talks between the two countries collapsed acrimoniously in August, according to the Straits Times.

should_know.headline: Bank of England set to raise rates to 4% this week as BOJ readies December hike
should_know.summary: The Bank of England is expected to raise its key rate to 4% on Thursday, joining peers in raising borrowing costs to contain a pickup in inflation ahead of an intense period of wage negotiations, according to the FT and WSJ. Reuters says the bank may push back on market bets for further rises. Reuters also reports the Bank of Japan has locked in a December hike, though uncertainty over the neutral rate clouds the outlook. The Guardian says more than 2.3m UK households face a sharp rise in mortgage payments in 2027 as they come off fixed deals.

should_know.headline: Anthropic plans $3.5bn share sale to Japan investors in IPO, filing shows
should_know.summary: Anthropic plans to sell $3.5 billion of shares to Japanese investors as part of its initial public offering, according to a filing cited by Reuters. Le Monde reports the IPO document also details the "catastrophic or existential" risks the company says AI poses to humanity.

should_know.headline: China's party plenum document pledges digital tools against graft and deeper reach into tech sector
should_know.summary: The Communist Party's fifth plenum document says it will step up "party building" across China's tech sector and use digital tools to fight corruption, according to the South China Morning Post. Xi Jinping defended strict party discipline as a "fundamental guarantee" for China's rise that does not stifle growth. Nikkei Asia separately reports the party is turning to big-data surveillance against graft, and the SCMP says "unwritten rules" are a new target of the campaign.

should_know.headline: Freezer temperatures soar at Swedish and Belgian supermarkets; one store blames hackers
should_know.summary: Freezers at several Swedish grocery stores overheated overnight, ICA and Coop said on Monday, and at least one store blamed a cyberattack. Coop told Aftonbladet that six of its stores were affected; ICA said a limited number of its stores were hit. The Financial Times reports overheating as high as 55C in dozens of stores in Sweden and Belgium, weeks after French police said hackers seized cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets.

should_know.headline: Oleshky truce ends as Kyiv and Moscow each say the other used it to reinforce
should_know.summary: The six-day local ceasefire around Russian-held Oleshky expired at midnight Moscow time on Sunday, after Ukraine evacuated 167 civilians, including 22 children, from threatened parts of Kherson region. On Monday, Ukraine's General Staff said Russian forces used the pause to strengthen their positions, while the Kremlin said it assumed Ukraine's army used it to regroup, which it called normal practice. The truce, mediated by US first lady Melania Trump with Pope Leo's involvement, was the longest local pause in fighting since the 2022 invasion; Pope Leo hopes it can aid wider peace efforts.
